reason: The commit changes recursive object-update behavior to track parent objects and reject loops, while the existing harness only parses bytes with json_loadb and serializes the resulting value. It never calls json_object_update_recursive or deep-copy APIs, and loader-produced JSON cannot exercise the programmatically constructed cyclic object graphs targeted by the new parents-set logic. The harness therefore needs a path that constructs multiple objects, optionally creates reference cycles, and invokes the affected recursive operation.
evidence: H0 invokes only json_loadb followed by json_dumps or json_dump_callback.
json_object_update_recursive now initializes a hashtable_t parents_set and delegates to do_object_update_recursive.
do_object_update_recursive adds jsonp_loop_check(parents, other, ...) and propagates recursive-update failures.
The changed deep-copy helpers also manage loop-tracking cleanup, but H0 does not invoke any deep-copy API.
The required cyclic/shared in-memory object state is not controllable through H0's serialized JSON input alone.
recommended_action: Extend or add a harness mode that programmatically builds destination and source object graphs from fuzz input, permits nested/shared/cyclic references with safe ownership handling, and calls json_object_update_recursive; also exercise json_deep_copy if the deep-copy cleanup changes are in scope.
